status: proposed 2026-09-28 at the owner's request ("shrines near towns that people visit. Small, local, believable, not legendary shrines."); built as data and functions by tools/shrines.py, not yet seen in any world
note: Wayside shrines on the approaches of towns people pass through: not every town, only where one fits the town's purpose (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md) and its road. Each is a few to a few dozen vanilla blocks. Their stories and dedications are Codex's: each has a neutral working name and "story": "for Codex", and nothing here says more than the look does.

fields.id: unique, lowercase; the function is cobblers:shrines/<id>
fields.name: a neutral working name, for Codex to replace
fields.settlement: the town whose approach it stands on (data/towns.json id)
fields.approach: the road it stands beside: a data/routes.json route id, or where a rest stop is reached from
fields.at: [x, z] of the shrine's centre column; its floor is the highest heightmap ground under it plus one
fields.facing: the side its front (the offerings) faces: north | east | south | west, towards the road
fields.palette: block states per part of the kind, overriding its defaults; each block id must be in `blocks`
fields.why: why a shrine of this kind stands here, from the town's purpose and the road

rules.note: Clearances in blocks, enforced by tools/shrines.py and checked again, independently, by tools/shrines_audit.py

blocks.note: Every block a shrine may write. Vanilla 1.21.1 only; tools/shrines_audit.py checks each id against the 1.21.1 client jar's blockstates and against data/spawn_blocks.json. The potted plants are their own block ids (minecraft:potted_*), none a spawn condition; the flowers themselves (minecraft:poppy and the rest) are, and are not used.

shrines.name: the Route 1 cairn (working name)
shrines.why: Brock's is the plateau's masons' town (docs/world-building/TOWN_CHARACTER.md). Where Route 1 comes up from the hometown and first reaches it, south-west of the town, a cairn of the masons' cut stone (stone brick, polished andesite, tuff) with a chiseled capstone, a candle, a pot and a cut slab on its front ledge, facing the road.

shrines.name: the Route 2 lantern stone (working name)
shrines.why: Misty's is the lake town that takes in whoever the water brings, and keeps a lantern at its lookout's head (TOWN_CHARACTER.md). Where Route 2 arrives from Brock's town, south-east of the town, a standing stone in the town's prismarine with a lit lantern on its head and potted flowers and candles at its foot, facing the road.

shrines.name: the fork niche below Surge's town (working name)
shrines.approach: the fork below the town's shelf, where route_03_misty_to_surge comes in and route_04_surge_to_erika leaves
shrines.why: Surge's is the signal town under Mt Vessu, built in the flank's deepslate with copper for its gear (TOWN_CHARACTER.md). Below its shelf the two roads part, one to Misty's lake and one on to Erika's; in the wedge between them, a roofed niche of deepslate brick open towards the town, a chiseled copper block in its back wall, a candle and a hanging lantern inside.

shrines.name: the Route 5 niche (working name)
shrines.why: Koga's is the fen-edge watch town, built in mud brick and mangrove (TOWN_CHARACTER.md). Where Route 5 arrives from Erika's town, north-west of the town, a roadside niche of mud brick under a mangrove roof, a candle and a hanging lantern in it and a potted fern beside it, open to the road.

shrines.name: the brow trail altar (working name)
shrines.approach: the brow trail up from route_08_blaine_to_giovanni to the stop (derived/towns/tableland_stop_plan.json brow_trail)
shrines.why: The Tableland stop is a waystation on the badlands plateau, reached from Route 8 by the brow trail (SETTLEMENTS.md, TOWN_CHARACTER.md). Near the top of the trail, west of it and short of the stop, a small roofed altar in the stop's red sandstone, open on its four sides, candles on the altar and a pot behind it, facing the trail and the road below.

shrines.name: the cirque path cairn (working name)
shrines.approach: the foot of the cirque path up from route_04_surge_to_erika to the hut (derived/towns/merian_hut_plan.json cirque_path)
shrines.why: The Merian hut is the keeper's hut at the river's source, a bed kept ready at the end of a long walk (TOWN_CHARACTER.md). Where the cirque path leaves Route 4 for the hut, east of the path's foot, a cairn of the hut's cobblestone, part mossy, with a lantern, a candle and a potted spruce on its front ledge, facing the path.
